subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should OpenClaw permanently treat ClawHub, bundled metadata, and official-catalog mappings as prompt-free provenance while requiring `--force` for arbitrary direct first installs and refusing those sources in Crestodian?
rationale: Tests prove implementation behavior, but they cannot decide which registries and owner-controlled metadata deserve prompt-free trust or whether broadening the public `--force` contract is the intended upgrade policy.

options.title: Approve the layered taxonomy
options.body: Accept the proposed prompt-free sources, retain separate ClawHub release-risk and install-policy checks, and land after an exact-head refresh.

options.title: Narrow the trusted set
options.body: Keep the central classifier but require acknowledgement for community ClawHub packages or another disputed source class before merge.

options.title: Separate acknowledgement semantics
options.body: Use a dedicated provenance-confirmation flag instead of broadening `--force`, preserving its current overwrite and `--link` contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the layered taxonomy
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed prompt-free sources, retain separate ClawHub release-risk and install-policy checks, and land after an exact-head refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to plugin install persistence, security hardening, and permanent plugin contract choices.
